home.title: Vespertine: surround and hi-res music player for Mac
home.description: Free, open-source Mac player for surround and hi-res collections: SACD and DVD-Video disc images, DSD, DTS CDs, DTS-HD MA, TrueHD and Dolby Atmos files, Spatial Audio on AirPods, and a bit-perfect signal path you can inspect.
home.ogAlt: Vespertine: the free, open-source Mac player for surround and hi-res music. Its signal path shows a 24-bit / 96 kHz FLAC playing bit-perfect on a Fosi Audio ZD3. Version {version}, macOS {minMacOS} or later.

hero.titleSr: Surround and hi-res music, on your Mac.
hero.lede: The free, open-source Mac player for surround and hi-res music collections. SACD and DVD-Video disc images, DSD, DTS CDs, DTS-HD MA, TrueHD and Atmos files share one library with your stereo albums, with head-tracked Spatial Audio on AirPods. A signal path shows each step from file to output. In English and {languages} other languages.

features.title: Built for your surround collection.
features.text: Surround and stereo music in one library, and a player that shows exactly what it did to the signal.
features.badgesLabel: Signal path states the app shows

pillars.title: Surround in one library
pillars.text: SACD images and rips, DVD-Video discs, DTS CDs, DTS-HD MA and TrueHD sit next to your stereo albums and play as head-tracked Spatial Audio on AirPods. When an album comes in both, each song is listed once and the right version plays for your output.

pillars.title: A signal path you can check
pillars.text: Rates, word lengths, gain and channel processing, read back from Core Audio. The bit-perfect conditions are in the source, with automated tests, a loopback test and a hardware verification guide.

pillars.title: Checks hi-res files
pillars.text: Analysis flags padded bit depth and possible upsampling or lossy origin. Spectral verdicts are estimates, shown with their evidence and limits. The same analysis runs on a Linux server next to your files.

pillars.title: Open source you can audit
pillars.text: Free under the GPL. Read, build and change the player, including its output conditions and tests. No account, subscription, ads or telemetry.

signal-path.title: Every track at its native rate and depth.
signal-path.lede: The signal path lists each step from the file to your DAC, read back from Core Audio, and says when something changed the samples.
body: Vespertine switches the device to each file’s rate and resamples, with Apple’s mastering-quality converter, only when the DAC can’t run it. BIT-PERFECT appears only when the conditions in the source are met: a native rate, nothing changing the samples, a word length that fits, and a device that is exclusive or not shared with another app. PCM playback has been tested up to 384 kHz on a FiiO K11.
list: Exclusive (hog) mode keeps other apps off the device. In shared mode the volume keys and the Digital Crown adjust your DAC; in exclusive mode they can too, if you turn that on.
Integer mode sends unprocessed 32-bit PCM straight to DACs that take integers.
Match 16-bit sources (off by default) sends 16-bit files to DACs with a real 16-bit mode as 16-bit, not zero-padded.
Gapless, including CUE-sheet albums split from one file.
Remembers your DAC. If it isn’t connected, music plays on the best connected output and moves back when the DAC returns.
Outputs without a volume control of their own (HDMI, optical, line-out) can use Vespertine’s volume, chosen per output. Below 100% the labels say it’s no longer bit-perfect.
Hands your DAC back at the rate and depth it had before, when Vespertine quits.
A built-in loopback test compares every sample Vespertine sends to a virtual device. It’s a software check, labelled as one, and never changes the BIT-PERFECT badge.
signal-path.alt: Vespertine playing Lazar Berman’s Liszt, Années de pèlerinage, from a 24-bit / 96 kHz FLAC: the inspector marks it bit-perfect and exclusive on a Fosi Audio ZD3, with each step of the signal path.
signal-path.floatAlt: The loopback test sheet: 24-bit at 44.1 and 96 kHz, 16-bit padded and a gapless pair, each bit-exact.

surround.title: Your 5.1 discs, in the same library.
surround.lede: Multichannel music plays as head-tracked Spatial Audio on AirPods, or folds down by channel layout on a stereo DAC.
body: DTS CDs decode to 5.1. SACD images, extracted SACD tracks, multichannel FLAC, TrueHD and DTS-HD MA render as head-tracked Spatial Audio on AirPods or fold down on a stereo DAC. Dolby Digital Plus with Atmos uses macOS’s object renderer; TrueHD Atmos and DTS:X play their channel bed. Channel-for-channel output is experimental, untested on real receivers and multichannel USB DACs (one Sony TV over HDMI has been tested: see docs/DEVICES.md); reports wanted.
list: Stereo and surround versions of an album are listed once; Vespertine plays whichever suits the output, or the one you pin.

Dolby Digital, DD+ and DTS-CD receiver bitstream is experimental, untested on real receivers and multichannel USB DACs (one Sony TV over HDMI has been tested: see docs/DEVICES.md); reports wanted. Carrier tests use FFmpeg’s S/PDIF reader. TrueHD and DTS-HD MA passthrough is unsupported on macOS.
Export for Spatial Audio as binaural stereo for headphones or multichannel ALAC for Apple devices, with tags and artwork.
surround.alt: Elton John’s Goodbye Yellow Brick Road, a 24-bit / 88.2 kHz 5.1 album, playing as head-tracked Spatial Audio on AirPods Max, with the signal path and a meter for each channel.
surround.floatAlt: An album with stereo and 5.1 versions of each song, listed once.

discs.title: Play the disc image itself.
discs.lede: Point Vespertine at an SACD or DVD-Video image and it plays the music straight from it, with nothing mounted, extracted or written.
body: SACD .iso images play their stereo and 5.1 areas, DST-compressed or plain, titled from the disc’s own text. DST is decoded back to the exact DSD, so stereo goes to your DAC as native DSD over DoP where the DAC supports it, and 5.1 plays as head-tracked Spatial Audio on AirPods. The LPCM music on DVD-Video discs (an .iso or a VIDEO_TS folder) plays bit for bit, one album per title and a track per chapter.
list: Matched sacd_extract bit for bit on two real discs. Discs with a 5.0 area, only a multichannel area, or DSD128 and above are covered only by synthesized test images so far.

DSF and DSDIFF from DSD64 to DSD512, DST-compressed DSDIFF included, go out as DoP to DACs that take the carrier rate, or convert to high-rate PCM. DoP is confirmed on a FiiO K11; carrier rates above 384 kHz are untested on hardware.
DVD-Video LPCM at 16, 20 and 24 bits, 48 and 96 kHz, up to 8 channels. DVD-Audio isn’t supported, and encrypted (CSS) discs need a decrypted copy.
discs.alt: Brothers In Arms by Dire Straits playing straight from its SACD disc image: stereo DSD64 over DoP to a FiiO K11, with the NATIVE DSD · DoP badge and the decoder reading SACD image, DST (lossless).
discs.floatAlt: Claudja Barry’s Love for the Sake of Love as DSD128 over DoP to a Fosi Audio ZD3, at 352.8 kHz.

analysis.title: Find out which “hi-res” files aren’t.
analysis.lede: Every file can be analyzed for its real bit depth, its real bandwidth and the fingerprints of lossy encoders and resamplers.
body: Verdicts come with their evidence and name what else could explain it, and a Suspect Hi-Res playlist collects them. Only zero padding is exact: the spectral verdicts are flagged as questions, because some high-bitrate lossy files pass as genuine and steep mastering filters, FM sources and tape or vinyl transfers can look suspicious. While music plays, meters and a live spectrum show what’s going out, DoP included.
list: 16-bit audio padded into 24-bit containers
Likely upsampled CD-quality masters sold as 96 or 192 kHz
Likely lossy origin: MP3 or AAC transcoded to FLAC
Likely synthetic high frequencies from SBR or “AI enhancement”
vespertine-analyze runs the same analysis on a Linux server next to your files; the app imports the results.
analysis.note: The file in this screenshot is a deliberate fake: the trailer’s own music, encoded to MP3 and upsampled to 24/192 under a made-up band name.
links: How the analysis works, and where it misses
analysis.alt: The Analysis tab flagging a 24/192 “remaster” as a likely lossy origin: its long-term spectrum stops at 16 kHz.

airpods.title: Lossless on AirPods Max, and it says so.
airpods.lede: Connected with the USB-C cable, AirPods Max are recognized as a 24-bit / 48 kHz lossless device.
body: 48 kHz music plays bit-perfect and everything else is converted with Apple’s mastering-quality resampler, in plain view. Over Bluetooth, Vespertine tells you the link is AAC. This rests on Apple’s description of the cable path and Core Audio’s readback, since AirPods have no digital output to loop back.
airpods.alt: A smart playlist of 24-bit / 48 kHz tracks, narrowed to Oasis, playing bit-perfect on AirPods Max over USB-C.

library.title: Browse like Apple Music. Manage like a librarian.
library.lede: Albums, artists, songs and genres, each with filters you can combine, and Shuffle for any of them.
list: Filters for format, 24-bit, 88.2 kHz and up, multichannel, genre, year, sample rate, channels and analysis verdict. Search ignores case and accents.
Smart playlists in the units you think in: 24-bit, 88.2 kHz.
Remasters, mono and stereo releases and SACDs of one album share a card; choose the edition when you open it.
Favorites and play counts, kept in the library and never written to your files. Imports M3U and Apple Music playlists, play counts and favorites.
Tag editor with backups and one-step revert, plus MusicBrainz enrichment that shows its confidence before writing anything.
Network shares over SMB, NFS or WebDAV, with caching, Keep Offline and playback built for slow servers.
Find Music searches every drive for your real music and leaves the clutter behind. A short setup on first launch picks your output and explains what exclusive access and ReplayGain do.
Parametric EQ per output that imports AutoEQ and Equalizer APO presets. Off by default; when it’s on, the signal path says EQUALIZER instead of BIT-PERFECT.
Mini player, menu-bar extra, media keys, ReplayGain and automatic, signed updates.
library.alt: The Genres page: a tile per genre with a mosaic of its covers.

languages.title: Speaks your language.
languages.lede: Every menu, setting and signal-path message is translated into {languages} languages besides English.
body: From Ukrainian, German and Japanese to Swahili, Tamil and Hausa, with local plurals and number formats, and Simplified, Traditional and Hong Kong Chinese each with their own vocabulary. Arabic, Hebrew, Persian and Urdu get a right-to-left layout.

How the translations are checked: an automatic check on every change confirms every string in the app exists in all {languages} languages with the same placeholders and the plural forms each language needs, and every screen was reviewed in every language for clipped or overlapping text and right-to-left mirroring. They began as careful machine translations, so corrections from native speakers are very welcome on GitHub.
languages.alt: Vespertine written in each of its {languagesTotal} interface languages, from ヴェスパタイン and Веспертайн to فسبرتاين and वेस्परटाइन, at mixed sizes and typefaces.

formats.title: Surround, lossless and lossy files.
formats.text: Stereo and multichannel, PCM and DSD, disc images and plain files, with CUE sheets throughout.
formats.caption: Formats Vespertine plays, and how

rows.name: FLAC, ALAC, WAV, AIFF
rows.text: Native rate and depth up to 32-bit and the rate your DAC runs (tested to 384 kHz); unchanged 32-bit PCM needs integer mode. CUE-sheet images.

rows.name: DSD64 – DSD512
rows.text: DSF and DSDIFF, DST-compressed or plain. DoP depends on the DAC and carrier rate, otherwise PCM. DoP carrier rates above 384 kHz are untested on hardware.

rows.name: SACD images
rows.text: Stereo and multichannel areas, DST or plain, straight from the image; each song listed once with its stereo and 5.1 versions.

rows.name: DVD-Video LPCM
rows.text: 16, 20 and 24-bit at 48 and 96 kHz, 1 to 8 channels, bit for bit; one album per title, a track per chapter. DVD-Audio isn’t supported.

rows.name: Dolby Atmos
rows.text: Dolby Digital Plus with Atmos, rendered by macOS’s object renderer, or its decoded channel bed.

rows.name: Dolby TrueHD, MLP
rows.text: Lossless, can be bit-perfect; TrueHD Atmos plays its channel bed, its objects aren’t rendered.

rows.name: DTS-HD Master Audio, DTS-HD HR, DTS
rows.text: MA is lossless and can be bit-perfect; DTS:X plays its channel bed. Raw DTS decodes; DTS-CD bitstream is a separate path.

rows.name: Dolby Digital (Plus)
rows.text: Decoded by macOS. Receiver bitstream is experimental, untested on real receivers and multichannel USB DACs (one Sony TV over HDMI has been tested: see docs/DEVICES.md); reports wanted.

rows.name: DTS CDs and DTS-WAV
rows.text: Recognized and decoded to 5.1, including CUE-split albums.

rows.name: APE, WavPack, TTA
rows.text: Lossless. DSD inside WavPack isn’t supported.

compare.title: How it stacks up.
compare.intro: Several Mac players offer bit-perfect playback. This compares what each player’s own documentation or source code says. “Not documented” means the vendor doesn’t say either way, not that the feature is missing. Vespertine has no convolution, audio effect plugins or streaming services.
compare.caption: Vespertine compared with seven other Mac music players, from each player’s own documentation or source
rows: Apple Spatial Audio for local surround
notes: ¹ Apple Music on macOS 27 was bit-exact at 16/24-bit in third-party loopback tests reported on ASR, at 100% volume. This is not a Vespertine measurement; the original report could not be independently rechecked for this update. There is still no automatic rate switching, hog mode, FLAC or DSD on Mac.
² Multichannel DAC output and receiver bitstream are experimental, untested on real receivers and multichannel USB DACs (one Sony TV over HDMI has been tested: see docs/DEVICES.md); reports wanted.
³ Apple documents Spatial Audio with head tracking for Dolby Atmos tracks in the Apple Music catalog, not spatial rendering of your own multichannel files.

⁴ Tested on foobar2000 2.26 (macOS 27.0.1), with no components: DSF, DFF and SACD ISO files fail with “Unsupported file format”. DSF and DFF play only as 352.8 kHz PCM after installing FFmpeg separately and adding them to its FFmpeg Decoder Wrapper; SACD ISO still fails.
compare.sources: Sources and scope. Corrections welcome: open an issue.

whatsNew.title: What’s new in {version}.
whatsNew.meta: already installed? It updates itself, or {brewUpgrade}
whatsNew.inEnglish: These release notes haven’t been translated yet, so they are shown in English.

items.a: Yes. Vespertine is free and open source under the GPL-3.0. There’s no account, no subscription, no ads and no telemetry (privacy). It only goes online to check for updates, and to reach MusicBrainz, the Cover Art Archive or ListenBrainz, or to find covers for your Discord status, when you ask it to.
macOS {minMacOS} ({minMacOSName}) or later, on Apple silicon or Intel. Intel hardware is untested; the Intel build has run under Rosetta, and reports from real Intel Macs are welcome.

items.q: How do I install and update it?
items.a: Download the DMG, open it and move Vespertine to Applications. It’s signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple, and it updates itself; every update is signed. With Homebrew: {brew}, then {brewUpgrade} or the app’s own updates.

items.q: Does it stream from Qobuz, TIDAL or Apple Music?
items.a: No. Vespertine plays music you own, on your Mac, on external drives or on a network share. DRM-protected Apple Music subscription downloads cannot be played.

items.q: How do I know it’s actually bit-perfect?
items.a: The signal path reads back what Core Audio actually did: the device’s nominal rate, its physical format and who holds it. The decoders have automated tests (TrueHD against its source, DTS against FFmpeg’s own decoder), a built-in loopback test checks the software path sample by sample, and vespertine-probe lets you check your own hardware. How to verify it yourself.

items.q: Can it play SACD and DVD discs?
items.a: It plays their images. SACD .iso images, stereo and multichannel, DST-compressed or plain, and the LPCM music on DVD-Video images or VIDEO_TS folders play straight from the image, with nothing extracted. DVD-Audio isn’t supported, and encrypted (CSS) DVDs need a decrypted copy.

Dolby Digital Plus with Atmos plays through macOS’s object renderer, as head-tracked Spatial Audio on AirPods. TrueHD Atmos and DTS:X play their lossless channel bed; their objects aren’t rendered. Bitstream to an AV receiver is experimental, untested on real receivers; reports wanted.
Only when you edit tags, and then each file is backed up first and can be reverted in one step. Folders are referenced in place; importing makes APFS clones that take no extra space.

items.q: Which hardware has it been tested on?
items.a: Playback has been tested on a FiiO K11 at rates up to 384 kHz, with DoP and integer mode; AirPods Max over USB-C and Bluetooth; MacBook Pro speakers; and a Sony TV over HDMI in 5.1. Intel hardware is untested. Receiver bitstream and multichannel DAC output are experimental, untested on real receivers and multichannel USB DACs (one Sony TV over HDMI has been tested: see docs/DEVICES.md); reports wanted.

Probably: the interface is in English and {languages} other languages, including right-to-left Arabic, Hebrew, Persian and Urdu. Vespertine follows the language set for it in System Settings. Corrections from native speakers are welcome on GitHub.

privacy.title: Privacy: Vespertine collects nothing
privacy.description: The Vespertine app collects nothing: no accounts, analytics, telemetry, crash reporting or ads. What the app and this website connect to, and why.
privacy.ogAlt: Vespertine privacy: Vespertine collects nothing. No accounts, analytics, telemetry, crash reporting or advertising.
privacy.heading: Vespertine collects
privacy.updated: Effective {effective} (adds the optional Discord status). The “This website” section was updated on {statsUpdated}, when the site began counting visits with self-hosted, cookieless statistics, and on {langUpdated}, when the language menu began remembering your choice on your device.
privacy.intro: Vespertine is a free, open-source music player. The app has no accounts, no analytics, no telemetry, no crash reporting and no advertising. The developer receives no information about you or your music. Because the source code is public, you can check every statement on this page.
privacy.stays: Your library database, playlists, play counts, file analysis results, artwork cache and settings are stored in your user Library on your Mac. Passwords for network shares and your ListenBrainz token, if you add one, are stored in the macOS Keychain. None of it is uploaded anywhere.
online: Update checks. Vespertine asks GitHub for its update feed about once a day, and when you choose Check for Updates. GitHub sees your IP address, as with any download. You can turn automatic checks off in Settings.

MusicBrainz and Cover Art Archive. Only when you use Look Up on MusicBrainz or Enrich Metadata (Find Music on This Mac offers Enrich for the music it adds, as a checkbox you can clear), Vespertine sends the album, artist and track names it’s looking for to musicbrainz.org. With “Fetch cover art” on in Settings, it downloads covers from coverartarchive.org, which serves them from the Internet Archive (archive.org). MusicBrainz and the Cover Art Archive are run by the MetaBrainz Foundation.

ListenBrainz. Only if you turn on scrobbling and enter your token, Vespertine sends listenbrainz.org the songs you play: title, artist, album, duration and their MusicBrainz IDs when your files have them. It sends “playing now” when a song starts, and a listen with its time once you’ve heard half of it or four minutes.

Discord. Only if you turn on the Discord status in Settings, Vespertine tells the Discord app on your Mac, over a connection that stays on your Mac, what’s playing: title, artist, album, format and progress. Discord shows it as your status to the people who can see your activity. To show the album’s cover, Vespertine looks it up by name, because Discord can only show images from the web: on coverartarchive.org when your files carry a MusicBrainz release ID, otherwise in Apple’s iTunes Search (itunes.apple.com), which receives the artist and album names. Discord then downloads the cover from there. You can turn covers off, and your files and their covers are never uploaded.

Network shares. Vespertine connects to the servers you add, and nowhere else, to read your music. While a share is connected it checks every minute or so that the server still answers, and looks for new music every half hour (never while you’re playing from it).
website: This site is hosted on GitHub Pages, which may log visitors’ IP addresses; see GitHub’s privacy statement. The download buttons link to the app’s releases on GitHub. The site sets no cookies and loads its fonts, images and video from this site.

To learn which pages and buttons people use, the site counts visits with Umami, privacy-friendly software we run ourselves at stats.szeremeta.org. It sets no cookies, stores nothing on your device, doesn’t keep your IP address, and shares nothing with advertisers or any other company. It records the page, the site you came from, your approximate country, your browser, operating system, screen size and language, and clicks on the download, GitHub and Homebrew buttons. It can’t follow you across websites or identify you, and it skips visitors whose browser sends Do Not Track. The app never contacts it.

If you pick a language with the site’s language menu, your browser remembers the choice on your device (in its local storage), so the site doesn’t switch you back. It is never sent anywhere, and the site works the same without it.
privacy.changes: If this ever changes, this page and the release notes will say so first. Questions are welcome as a GitHub issue.

terms.license: Vespertine is free software under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or later. You may use it for any purpose, study and change its source code, and share copies, including modified ones, under the same license. It costs nothing, and there is nothing to sign up for.

0.14.0.summary: Vespertine 0.14.0 adds room correction: measure your speakers with a UMIK-1 microphone and play through filters made for your room. It also keeps network playback from running dry.
0.14.0.notes:
### Room correction
- **Measure your room.** Put a calibrated UMIK-1 microphone at the listening seat and Vespertine plays test sweeps through each speaker in turn, at 1 to 5 spots (5 by default: the seat, then left, right, in front and behind). It checks the level and the route to every speaker first, rejects a bad run and lets you retry or pick up where you left off. Stereo and 5.1 are both supported.
- **Filters for each speaker.** From the measurement Vespertine builds a small set of filters per speaker, mostly cuts for the bass peaks a room adds. Choose a target (Warm is the default, or Gentle tilt or Flat) and a range (bass only, or full range) and the filters are refitted from the stored measurement without measuring again. The graph shows what was measured, what is predicted after correction and the target, and the prediction is labeled as a prediction.
- **Delay and level alignment.** Each speaker's delay and level are measured too, so nearer speakers are held back until the farthest one's sound arrives and louder ones are turned down to the quietest.
- **Bring your own filters.** Import an Equalizer APO or REW filter file (per-speaker delay, level and filters), or import impulse responses (WAV, AIFF, CAF or FLAC) to play through as convolution filters. Export a profile as Equalizer APO text or as a Vespertine profile. Lines Vespertine can't play are refused with the line number rather than played as something else.
- **Off by default, so bit-perfect stays bit-perfect.** Room correction is switched on per output and is tied to the output it was measured on. While it changes the samples, the signal path says ROOM CORRECTION and the stream is no longer marked bit-perfect. With it off, playback is untouched. Integer mode and Match 16-bit stay off while it is on.
- **What it covers.** Stereo and 5.1 PCM that Vespertine renders. Dolby and DTS bitstreams, Atmos and other channel counts step aside, and the signal path says why. DSD on a DoP DAC is converted to PCM while correction is on so it is corrected too; tick Keep native DSD on that output to send it natively and uncorrected instead.
- **One window.** View → Room Correction, also from the Equalizer window and each output's settings, holds the switch, Measure, Import, Export, the profiles, the before and after graph, the target and range, and each speaker's delay, level and filters. This replaces the earlier beta Room Measurement window. The method is written up in `docs/ROOM-CORRECTION.md`.

### Network playback
- **Fewer dropouts from a NAS.** Tracks on a network share are now copied to your Mac before they play, and the next track is copied ahead, so a hiccup on the network no longer stops the music. Large DSD files are read in a way that keeps a long lead ready.
- **A loading ring on the play button.** While Vespertine waits for data from the network, the play/pause button shows a small turning ring (still when Reduce Motion is on). Short read failures are retried.
- **Limits.** A very long outage, or a link that is slower than the music, can still make playback pause to refill. Cached copies use at most 8 GB, and a source larger than that fails with a clear message. See `docs/NETWORK-PLAYBACK.md`.

### Also new
- **DoP on by default for known DACs.** The FiiO K11 and the Fosi Audio ZD3 start with DoP turned on. If you turn it off, Vespertine remembers.
- **Recently Added shows 150 albums**, up from 60, so a big import doesn't push the albums just before it off the list.
- **Fosi Audio ZD3.** The ZD3 is now in the supported-devices list and the website screenshots were retaken on it.
- **Website.** A "Star it on GitHub" and "Join the discussion" line sits under the download buttons.

### Verification
- The engine, library and app test suites pass, including new tests for the room filter design, for playback through the correction stage and the convolution filter, for the measurement steps against a simulated room, for the import formats and for the network cache. The real-time audio code is also checked under the address, thread and undefined-behavior sanitizers.
- Checked on real hardware: a full measurement with a UMIK-1 at the listening seat, the filters built from it, and playback through room correction on a Fosi Audio ZD3 with stereo speakers.

0.13.2.summary: Vespertine 0.13.2 plays 5.1 DSD in Spatial Audio on AirPods, tells you when audio is converted or downmixed, and no longer hangs on quit.
0.13.2.notes:
### Spatial Audio
- **5.1 DSD now plays in Spatial Audio.** A 5.1 DSD file (DSF, DSDIFF, DST-compressed DSDIFF or an SACD image) is converted to PCM and every channel is placed where it belongs, so the LFE and surround channels are no longer lost. Before, discrete DSDIFF channels could land on a three-speaker bed and the rear channels went missing.
- **It says what happened to the audio.** The signal path shows **DSD → PCM** next to SPATIAL or a downmix, and two new notices, "Converted from DSD" and "Downmixed to stereo", appear when they apply. Both are translated into all 44 languages.
- Checked by the developer on AirPods Max.

### Fixed
- **Quitting no longer hangs.** Cmd-Q could leave a spinning cursor while Vespertine waited on the audio device. It now quits right away.
- **Multichannel files read correctly.** RF64 and Wave64 files open properly, DSD channel names are read from the file, and discrete multichannel routing follows the file's own channel layout.

### Verification
- The engine, library and app test suites pass, including new tests that play each 5.1 DSD format through Spatial Audio and check that every channel arrives in its place. The left/right placement check runs on real Macs only; GitHub's test machines skip that one check.

0.13.1.summary: Vespertine now says when the equalizer can't change what's playing, offers an optional reference equalizer for each USB-C AirPods Max model, and has its first multichannel result on real hardware.

0.13.0.summary: Vespertine now keeps a history of what you've played, gives Up Next its own panel beside the library, shows every edition of an album on one card, and can show what you're playing as your Discord status.

0.12.2.summary: Vespertine now works properly in Light Mode, lets outputs without a volume control use Vespertine's volume, and keeps analyzing your library while you listen from a network share.

0.12.1.summary: Vespertine now plays smoothly from slow network shares, analyzes big libraries faster with shares included, plays hi-res on small USB-C DACs at the highest rate they offer, and keeps the keyboard and multi-selections where you expect them.

0.12.0.summary: Vespertine now plays DST-compressed DSDIFF files and the LPCM music on DVD-Video discs natively, keeps every track of EAC CUE sheets, and starts songs from a network share right away even while a library scan is running.
